'''Catherine Peichel''' is an American geneticist who works at the Division of Evolutionary Ecology department of the [[University of Bern]]. Her research focuses on the [[genes|genetic]] bases of speciation, adaptation, and [[Phenotype|phenotypic]] diversity, as well as the [[Sex chromosome|evolution of sex chromosomes]]. Much of her research uses three-spined stickleback fish (''[[Gasterosteus aculeatus]]'') as models, both in the lab and in wild populations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-09 |title=Prof. Dr. Catherine (Katie) Peichel |url=https://www.ee.iee.unibe.ch/about_us/team/persons/prof_dr_peichel_catherine_katie/index_eng.html |access-date=2024-09-27 |website=unibe.ch}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Burroughs Wellcome Fund|Burroughs Wellcome Career Award]] in the Biomedical Sciences in 2003 for her significant contributions in developing the stickleback as a model system for evolutionary genetics.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Catherine Peichel|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/catherine-peichel/ |access-date=2024-09-27 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite report |url=https://www.bwfund.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/11/2002-Annual-Report.pdf |title=2002 Annual Report |author=Burroughs Wellcome Fund |date=2002 |author-link= |access-date=2024-09-27}}</ref>

Peichel was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-27 |title=Catherine L. Peichel |website=American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/catherine-l-peichel |access-date=2024-09-27 |language=en}}</ref> and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Catherine L. Peichel – NAS |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/catherine-l-peichel-0rjyzl/ |access-date=2024-09-27 |website=National Academy of Sciences}}</ref>
